NONE: B1 the part in the middle of the arm where it bends, or the part of a piece of clothing that covers this area
› disapproving to push someone rudely with your elbows so that you can move or have more space
› to hit someone with your elbow, sometimes as a sign to make them notice or remember something
（爲讓某人注意或提醒某事而）用肘碰

example: Her arm was bandaged from the elbow to the fingers.
她的手臂從肘部一直到手指全部纏上了繃帶。
The sleeve of his shirt was torn at the elbow.
他襯衫的肘部被撕了個洞。
He elbowed his way to the front of the crowd.
他們把旁觀者推到一邊。
She elbowed me in the ribs before I could say anything.
我還沒開口呢，她就用肘在我肋部碰了一下。
The polish needs a certain amount of elbow grease to apply.
要把這個擦亮得費不少勁。

NONE: › freedom to do what you want

example: We were tightly squashed in at dinner, with very little elbow room.
吃晚飯時，我們一個緊挨著一個在餐桌旁就坐，擠得幾乎一點空間都沒有。
At first the management gave the new director plenty of elbow room.
最初，管理階層給了新主管足夠的自主行事空間。

NONE: › to force someone or something out of a position or job
排擠；強行使…離開（職位或工作）

example: He resigned before he was elbowed out.
他不等被別人排擠出去，就自己先辭了職。
